recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should use a new tracker only if implementers still find the current element definition unclear; the FHIR-32581 requirement is already represented in build-scope source and reinforced by the later FHIR-39687 no-change decision.
issue_request: FHIR-32581 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO change request asking the spec to explain why DocumentReference.securityLabel and DocumentReference.meta.security can both exist, when they can differ, and how each should be used.
initial_application: The older definition already distinguished the referenced document labels from meta.security. Git commit 1e542148c2d27a0394c2798fa8a1a78014db1b4d expanded the build-scope StructureDefinition definition with the URL/content, data-elements, referenced-document, and sensitive-document/metadata explanation; commit 314c3b3a9f56c4480808c133aec77d1078f3bf6f later changed only may to might.
additional_context: DocumentReference is active in source/fhir.ini. OO Confluence minutes show the issue moving from a request for John Moehrke to write a better description to Persuasive with Modification and block-vote approval. Later FHIR-39687 asked to remove DocumentReference.securityLabel as duplicative, but was resolved Not Persuasive because FHIR-32581 had already clarified the distinction; the associated Zulip thread states the same distinction.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative source already explains that meta.security labels the data elements in DocumentReference while securityLabel labels the document the reference refers to, including why the referenced document can be more sensitive than its metadata.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published work renamed DocumentReference.confidentiality to securityLabel and introduced the original meta.security distinction that FHIR-32581 later expanded.
Later Resolved - No Change issue rejected removing DocumentReference.securityLabel because the FHIR-32581 clarification showed it is not a duplicate of meta.security.
Same DocumentReference.securityLabel element, but the issue concerns binding strength/value-set coherence rather than the meta.security distinction.
